newsitem.title: USA: Mass judge wants "nauseating detail" on legal fees.
newsitem.headline: Mass judge wants "nauseating detail" on legal fees.

text.p: A Massachusetts state judge Monday told attorneys who repesented creditors of the now abolished Middlesex County they would have to seek attorney fees from the state in "nauseating detail."

Middlesex Superior Court Judge Hiller Zobel denied a request by attorney Tom Gass of Palmer & Dodge, who represented two of the county's creditors, Fleet Financial Group and Mellon Bank Corp unit Dreyfus Corp, to submit his bill to the judge in his chambers or in camera.
"If you want to get paid, you will have to put in nauseating detail, what it is you did and why you should get paid," the judge said.

Governor William Weld last Friday signed a bill abolishing Middlesex County, home of Cambridge-based Harvard University and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. As a result, the state took over all county assets and liabilities.
The county defaulted on about $4.5 million of revenue anticipation notes in December, which were owned by Fleet and Dreyfus.
Weld wants to eliminate all counties in the state, saying his Administration could run them more efficiently and at a lower cost.
